baseline_models.focus_anchor: The contrast between taking awliya apart from God and the emphatic declaration that God is al-Wali, followed by His reviving the dead and power over every thing.
baseline_models.mechanism: Taking is active acquisition, while wilaya can be charge of an affair as well as support. The repeated huwa links true wilaya to two tests no acquired patron can satisfy: restoring life after power has gone and exercising effective capacity over the whole field of things.

activation_trace.role: Acquisition or making something one's own casts the rival patrons as offices their users manufacture for themselves.
Otherness or lower rank marks those acquired offices as substitutes outside the divine claim.
Taking charge of an affair supplies the governing office denied to the adopted patrons and asserted for God.
Animate life makes enlivening an operative demonstration of the true Wali's agency.
Loss of life and force supplies the terminal condition that divine guardianship alone reverses.
Effective capacity reaching action and possession closes the contrast with patrons whose office has no such reach.

changed_reading.before: People chose protectors besides God, whereas God alone protects and can resurrect.
changed_reading.after: The verse attacks manufactured proxy jurisdictions: only God's nondelegable custody proves operational across the loss of life and across every possible object.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Min dunihi and the paired plural and singular forms of wali.
baseline_models.mechanism: Dun can picture what is nearer yet short of the goal, while wilaya can be adjacency without a gap. Read together, the supposed intermediaries are selected as convenient near points but remain short of the reach they promise; the emphatic singular Wali reverses that spatial intuition.

activation_trace.role: Nearness that still falls short supplies the spatial defect of the substitute patrons.
Adjacency without an intervening gap makes true wilaya immediate rather than intermediary.
Death supplies the maximal apparent separation that the true Wali's nearness can cross.
Unrestricted effective capacity prevents divine nearness from being merely affective or spatial.

changed_reading.before: Min dunihi simply means besides Him.
changed_reading.after: The phrase also exposes a failed shortcut: patrons chosen as nearer access points remain short of the goal, while the true Wali is immediately operative even across death.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The direct sequence al-Wali, He gives life to the dead.
baseline_models.mechanism: The death inventory includes a heart without intelligence, and life can name benefit or rescue from destruction. Their placement after supportive wilaya permits a second register alongside bodily resurrection: patronage restores a faculty that has become inert.

activation_trace.role: Love, support, and alliance give the Wali a restorative relation to the one supported.
Life as benefit and rescue permits enlivening to restore effective human capacity.
A deadened heart lacking intelligence supplies the inner state that can be revived.
Restored capability makes the inner-life reading functional rather than a loose metaphor.

changed_reading.before: Giving life to the dead refers only to bodily resurrection.
changed_reading.after: Without displacing bodily resurrection, the sequence can also present the Wali as restoring deadened understanding and useful agency.

context_deltas.mechanism: The exact adopted-awliya formula occurs at 42:6, where God's guarding remains in force while the messenger is denied the role of wakil over them. This turns al-Wali at 42:9 into a boundary of responsibility: ultimate custody is divine and is not transferred even to the messenger.

activation_trace.role: Taking charge of an affair anchors the focus claim as an office of custody.
The repeated patron term carries the same claimed office into the explicit custody contrast.
Watching and guarding identify the divine side of the responsibility boundary.
The one who sufficiently manages and preserves names precisely the role denied to the messenger.

structural_cues: 42:6 repeats the focus's adopted-awliya wording, then coordinates divine hifz with the denial that the addressee is their wakil.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the exact repetition and the hifz versus not-wakil contrast; I infer that it partitions ultimate custody from prophetic responsibility. A live alternative is that it only denies coercive enforcement, not every delegated form of care.

changed_reading.before: God is the best or only protector among possible protectors.
changed_reading.after: God's wilaya is nontransferable custody, while even the messenger's task stops short of guaranteeing or managing persons' outcomes.

context_deltas.mechanism: The Wali's charge becomes juridical as every disputed thing is returned to God's judgment at 42:10, while 42:21 depicts partners entering norm-setting without divine authorization. Adopted awliya can therefore be rival sources of binding order, not only hoped-for rescuers.

activation_trace.role: Governance of an affair anchors wilaya as an authority-bearing office.
Judgment between people gives the divine office an adjudicative function.
Reliant entrustment shows the practical response to that jurisdiction.
Partnership supplies the rival authority structure that competes with exclusive wilaya.
Entry into an affair figures the partners' intrusion into the domain of norm-setting.
Permission marks authorization as the missing condition of the partners' religious ordering.

structural_cues: 42:10 sends whatever is disputed to God for judgment.
The interrogative at 42:21 echoes the focus's interrogative and asks whether partners instituted in religion what God did not authorize.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies divine adjudication and unauthorized partner-made religion; I infer that these partners instantiate the governing side of adopted awliya. Alternatively, the focus may target cultic patronage while 42:21 names a separate legal error.

changed_reading.before: The false awliya are mainly objects from which protection is expected.
changed_reading.after: They also function as self-authorized jurisdictions whose judgments and norms displace the Wali to whom disputed affairs belong.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus's qadir first reads as unrestricted ability. At 42:12, spreading provision is paired with constricting it; at 42:27, unlimited spread would produce transgression, so descent occurs by a measure. Power in the Wali's life-giving office is thus controlled calibration, not maximum output.

activation_trace.role: Effective capacity supplies the focus's overt assertion of power.
A quantity reaching its proper limit keeps measure latent inside the same power root.
Expansion against contraction supplies one pole of the calibrated provision mechanism.
Constriction to a smaller allotment supplies the counter-pole to expansion.
Transgressing a limit supplies the stated harm that unbounded expansion would enable.
A determined measure becomes the protective limit by which provision descends.

structural_cues: 42:12 places expansion and constriction of provision in direct coordination.
42:27 gives a counterfactual causal sequence: unrestricted provision would lead to transgression, but provision descends by measure.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the shared root, the expansion-constriction pair, and the causal warning about excess; I infer that qadir in the focus carries an administrative resonance of setting viable measures. Alternatively, the adjective of ability and the verb of constriction may remain semantically separate here.

changed_reading.before: Qadir adds a general claim of unlimited power after resurrection.
changed_reading.after: Qadir also characterizes protective power as exact apportionment: the Wali sustains life by expanding, withholding, and setting limits appropriate to consequences.

context_deltas.mechanism: At 42:28, rain arrives after hope is cut off, mercy is spread, and God is then named al-Wali. Focus branches already join life to rain-fed land and death to uncultivated ground. The focus's resurrection clause becomes a compressed ecological and affective pattern of guardianship: restoration begins precisely after resources and hope appear exhausted.

activation_trace.role: Land living through rain and vegetation supplies the focus-side material model of revival.
Unworked dead ground supplies the reversible state answered by rain-life.
Life-giving rain supplies the material agent that turns dead land toward growth.
Aid at distress preserves the same rain event as rescue rather than mere weather.
Hope cut off supplies an affective analogue to the dead condition.
Rain reviving dried pasture supplies the opening and renewed spread of formerly inert life.
Merciful tenderness names the restorative event as an act of patronage.

structural_cues: 42:28 orders the event as rain after despair, spreading mercy, then the divine title al-Wali.
The focus likewise orders al-Wali immediately before giving life to the dead.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the two predicate sequences and explicit rain-life and dead-land branches; I infer that the later scene materializes the focus's wilaya-through-revival mechanism. Alternatively, rain may serve only as evidence for a future resurrection rather than broaden the present operation of wilaya.

changed_reading.before: Reviving the dead is chiefly a future proof that the claimed patrons lack.
changed_reading.after: Revival is also the Wali's recurring mode of timed rescue: dead ground and extinguished hope are reopened by mercy after ordinary prospects end.

context_deltas.mechanism: 42:29 moves from creating the heavens and earth, through broadcasting creatures within them, to the capacity to gather those creatures. That sequence gives the focus's revival claim a reversible material operation: the one Wali does not lose the members of a dispersed creation but can collect them after maximal distribution.

activation_trace.role: Charge over an affair anchors regathering as custodial rather than merely spectacular power.
Loss of life supplies the focus's terminal dispersed condition.
Bringing creation into being supplies the outbound side of the operation.
Scattering or broadcasting supplies maximal distribution across the created field.
Joining what was separated supplies the reverse transform that makes resurrection mechanically imaginable.
Effective capacity closes the creation-dispersion-gathering sequence with the same power term as the focus.

structural_cues: 42:29 places creation, dispersal of creatures, gathering, willing, and qadir in one ordered sentence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the outbound dispersion and inbound gathering under the repeated power root; I infer that this is the operational expansion of reviving the dead and that custody preserves identity across dispersal. Alternatively, gathering may denote assembly for judgment without specifying material reconstitution.

changed_reading.before: Revival is an isolated miracle demonstrating omnipotence.
changed_reading.after: Revival is the inverse of cosmic dispersal: the Wali who generated and broadcast every creature can retain and regather each one.

context_deltas.mechanism: 42:44-47 repeatedly combine absence of a wali with the search for a return, a path, or a refuge, then deny each exit. This makes the focus's Wali and reviver the sole agent of reversibility at a terminal boundary: ordinary patrons operate within available routes, but divine wilaya governs whether a closed state can be reopened.

activation_trace.role: Support and rescue anchor the Wali as the relation sought when every route fails.
Death supplies the focus's strongest closed state.
The denied supporter places failed wilaya directly beside the plea for return.
Return to a prior place or state supplies the reversal the condemned seek.
A traversable extended path supplies the missing route by which reversal might occur.
Repelling or turning something back marks the coming day as beyond creaturely reversal.
A shelter of recourse supplies the final protective alternative that the passage denies.

structural_cues: 42:44 places no wali before a plea for a route of return.
42:46 again denies awliya apart from God and then denies a path.
42:47 denies both reversal of the day and any refuge.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated no-wali, no-return, no-path, and no-refuge pattern; I infer that the focus defines true wilaya by control of reversibility itself. Alternatively, the later denials may describe judgment without adding a semantic component to al-Wali.

changed_reading.before: The Wali protects from danger within the ordinary course of events.
changed_reading.after: The Wali alone governs return from states with no creaturely exit, which explains why reviving the dead is the decisive specification of His patronage.

context_deltas.mechanism: 42:49-50 locates power within the unequal allocation of daughters, sons, pairings, and barrenness. The focus's life-giving Wali therefore governs generative openings and closures as gifts rather than transactions; true patronage is sovereign care, not a promise that the patron must deliver the desired family outcome.

activation_trace.role: Animate life anchors the focus claim in the domain of generated living beings.
Effective capacity anchors the closing examples as specifications of the focus's power.
A gift given without exchange makes offspring an allocation rather than payment for patronage.
Joining one thing as a mate to another supplies one possible generative arrangement.
Barrenness of womb and offspring supplies the contrasting closure within the same sovereign allocation.
The repeated capability term explicitly returns the generative alternatives to the focus's closing predicate.

structural_cues: 42:49-50 enumerate four reproductive outcomes under repeated willing and close with knowing and qadir.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies gift language, paired and barren outcomes, and the repeated qadir; I infer that these make life-giving power intimate while refusing a transactional model of wilaya. Alternatively, the outcomes may be examples of power only, without defining patronage.

changed_reading.before: Life-giving power concerns resurrection at the end of life.
changed_reading.after: It also governs present generative possibility, including gift and withholding, so the true Wali cannot be reduced to a guarantor of preferred outcomes.

context_deltas.mechanism: 42:51 transmits knowledge through hidden disclosure, a barrier, or a messenger; 42:52 then calls the disclosure a spirit and makes it light by which guidance occurs. Those supplied life and illumination mechanisms activate the focus branches of dead understanding and beneficial life: the Wali revives not only bodies but the capacity to know and move toward a path.

activation_trace.role: Life as benefit and rescue supplies the focus-side possibility of restored effective understanding.
A heart without intelligence supplies the precise inner deadness addressed by disclosure.
Hidden imparting of knowledge supplies the transmission that reaches an otherwise inaccessible interior.
A screening barrier supplies the separation across which life-giving knowledge still arrives.
The spirit by which bodily life exists supplies an explicit life-bearing image for revelation.
Illumination supplies restored visibility to the formerly unknowing faculty.
Gentle direction to a path turns restored perception into renewed movement.

structural_cues: 42:51 lists three mediated modes of divine speech despite separation.
42:52 identifies what was revealed as spirit, then as light that effects guidance toward a straight path.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies revelation as spirit and light, guidance, and a focus branch for dead intelligence; I infer a functional equivalence between disclosure and reanimation of understanding. Alternatively, bodily resurrection may remain the sole referent of the focus clause while guidance forms a separate life analogy.

changed_reading.before: The focus moves from patronage to bodily resurrection as an unrelated proof of power.
changed_reading.after: The predicates form a continuous office: the Wali crosses barriers to transmit spirit-like light, reviving deadened understanding into directed agency while retaining the bodily claim.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the rare rain branch of wali inside a divine title. It remains anchored because 42:28 names God al-Wali immediately after rain, despair, and spreading mercy, and the focus places the same title before revival. Downstream prose should present it only as a lexical-material reverberation, not as a replacement definition of the divine name.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Al-Wali at 42:9 and its immediate continuation with giving life to the dead.

activation_trace.role: Rain following the first seasonal rain supplies an unusual material cadence for the Wali who follows deprivation with renewal.
Rain from the sky makes the rare wali-rain branch locally concrete rather than free association.
Dried pasture revived by rain supplies the renewed land-state produced by the following rain.
The repeated title in the rain verse binds the rare branch back to the focus's central word.

changed_reading.before: Al-Wali names the protector who can revive.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the title also reverberates with a following rain: divine patronage arrives after prior resources fail and renews what had dried out.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is a cross-domain reading from organism to transport system. It remains anchored because the focus's death inventory explicitly includes a wind becoming still, while 42:33 makes wind cessation leave ships motionless after movement. Downstream prose should call it a material analogy for reversibility, not claim that the dead in 42:9 lexically means ships.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: He gives life to the dead at 42:9, with death carrying a stilling or quiescence branch.

activation_trace.role: A wind dying by becoming still supplies the focus-side bridge from death to arrested motion.
Life as restored benefit permits reanimation to mean renewed effective operation in the analogy.
Loss of motion supplies the causal intervention applied to the wind.
Wind or moving air supplies the external force whose withdrawal arrests the vessels.
Fixity after prior movement supplies the observable death-like state of the ships.

changed_reading.before: Revival means returning biological life after death.
changed_reading.after: As a contained material analogy, revival is also restoration of flow and agency to a system made inert when its animating force is stilled.

strongest_changes: The repeated formula at 42:6 makes al-Wali a nondelegable custody office and sharply limits prophetic responsibility.
The provision sequences at 42:12 and 42:27 revise qadir from sheer force into protective calibration by expansion, constriction, and measure.
Rain after despair and creation followed by dispersion and gathering make revival both ecological restoration and reversible regathering.
The no-return cluster at 42:44-47 and the spirit-light disclosure at 42:51-52 extend wilaya to reopening terminal states and restoring deadened understanding.
summary.what_was_special: Across the whole surah, the focus's three predicates behave as one mechanism: the true Wali retains custody, sets viable measures, and restores life or agency where substitutes encounter a closed boundary. The rare wali-as-following-rain branch becomes unusually live because a later divine title stands inside an explicit rain-restoration sequence.
remaining_uncertainties: The measured-power reading may be resonance across the q-d-r root rather than a semantic load carried by qadir in 42:9 itself.
The following-rain sense of wali is locally striking but remains branch-distant and should not displace the patronage sense.
Revelatory revival of dead understanding is well activated by the closing verses but may remain an analogy beside bodily resurrection rather than a second direct referent.
